title: Verifier‑Guided Generate→Validate→Repair for Intent‑Driven Network Configuration: A Confirmatory Study
abstract: We evaluate whether inserting a deterministic network verifier into an LLM‑driven generate→validate→repair pipeline reduces functional regressions and blast radius versus LLM‑alone proposals. Under a preregistered paired design (CNSM2026‑A1‑prereg‑v1; preregistration SHA‑256 feba320ea2e03679bd575ac3929f0dc060a5844982bec6758ac87d02a272eba3) we synthesized 200 stratified intent→configuration tasks and ran paired episodes with gpt‑5‑mini under two conditions: baseline (LLM‑alone) and guarded (LLM + deterministic_netops_validator_v5 + up to one automated repair iteration). On 188 complete pairs (376 completed episodes; 24 failed episodes) guarded vs baseline success rates were 1.000 and 0.9840425531914894 respectively; paired difference = 0.015957446808510634, 95% bootstrap percentile CI [0.0, 0.03723404255319149], exact McNemar two‑sided p = 0.25. The preregistered efficacy threshold (absolute change ≥ 0.20) was not met. Prespecified sensitivity (treating both‑missing pairs as failures) yields guarded_success = 188/200 = 0.94, baseline_success = 185/200 = 0.925, paired difference Δ = 0.015; preregistered bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed=1729) = [0.0, 0.035]. Repair activity was rare (repair invocations = 3) and corresponds to the three discordant guarded‑only successes (n_10 = 3). We release the full artifact bundle for reproducibility and provide deterministic extraction and bootstrap recipes referencing archived artifact checksums in the Disclosure Statement.

sections.introduction:
Motivation and question. Large language models (LLMs) are being proposed to translate operator intent into device configurations and to assist NetOps automation. Operational correctness requires more than syntactic plausibility: it requires preservation of invariants, bounded blast radius (limited collateral impact), and an auditable decision trail. A common architectural response is generate→validate→repair: an LLM proposes configuration(s), a deterministic verifier checks policy and functional invariants, and an automated repair routine attempts correction. Proposals such as tool‑assisted critiquing and verifier‑guided repair are promising in principle but their quantifiable operational benefit—when measured in a preregistered, paired within‑task design with full provenance—remains underexplored.

Research question and contributions. We ask: Does integrating a deterministic network verifier into an LLM‑driven generate→validate→repair pipeline reduce functional regressions and average blast radius versus LLM‑alone proposals on a seeded multi‑vendor synthetic benchmark? Contributions: (1) a preregistered paired confirmatory experiment (CNSM2026‑A1‑prereg‑v1; SHA‑256 feba320ea2e03679bd575ac3929f0dc060a5844982bec6758ac87d02a272eba3) comparing baseline (LLM‑alone) to guarded (LLM + deterministic_netops_validator_v5 + up to one automated repair); (2) a fully archived execution and analysis bundle (canonical input execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA‑256 = 8b1a66d7f2fc50404ff45d7ec16a30d3baae8f6b49572a3194fedbf3042da4d7) with per‑episode verifier traces and provider call artifacts; (3) confirmatory statistics (paired McNemar test and preregistered bootstrap CIs) and reproducible, deterministic recipes for the preregistered sensitivity bootstrap and repair‑invocation enumeration; (4) an artifact‑grounded failure analysis that explains why the preregistered efficacy threshold was not met and lists operational recommendations.
sections.related_work: Tool‑assisted critique and verifier literature. Prior work on tool‑augmented LLM correction (e.g., CRITIC [Gou et al., 2023]) and verifier‑based repair motivates closed‑loop pipelines where deterministic checks serve as a corrective oracle. Separate lines on formal/ensemble verification (e.g., SymNet; model‑checking approaches) show how deterministic analysis can provide rigorous reachability and policy validation. Recent applied NetOps studies (PreConfig, intent‑engines, intent translation) demonstrate LLM feasibility for configuration generation but highlight correctness and safety gaps that motivate verifier insertion. Surveys of LLMs for NetOps and intent engines document desiderata (auditability, verifier coverage, repair budgets) and report ceiling effects when baseline model correctness is high, which our results confirm in a preregistered paired setting. Our study differs by (a) preregistering a single precise estimand and analysis plan, (b) executing a paired within‑task design with full archived provenance, and (c) providing deterministic reproduction recipes tied to artifact checksums.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The preregistered plan CNSM2026‑A1‑prereg‑v1 (SHA‑256 feba320ea2e03679bd575ac3929f0dc060a5844982bec6758ac87d02a272eba3) specified the primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline computed on a deterministic validator correctness indicator. H1 required an absolute reduction in regression rate ≥ 0.20 (design power ≈ 0.80 with 200 pairs under preregistered discordant assumptions). The preregistration includes inclusion/exclusion rules, missingness handling, and the exact primary test: exact McNemar two‑sided inference with 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples; seed=1729). The preregistration record and execution manifest are archived (execution/execution_manifest.json; preregistration SHA‑256 above).

Synthetic benchmark and task generation. We used a deterministic Cornetto‑like multi‑vendor task generator (deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5). The confirmatory sample (200 paired tasks) was stratified across topology scales (small, medium, large) and vendor‑mix strata to cover common features (BGP, OSPF, static routes, VLAN, MTU) while restricting to constructs supported by deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Tasks flagged as unsupported were deterministically excluded and moved to exploratory buckets; the deterministic task manifest is archived (execution/task_manifest.jsonl SHA‑256 = bb87e31db6e08c4c874d082414d18e6edf7dc930d6fccbb0fb6a8c78346e4865). Representative per‑task payloads, required sequences, and golden expected_final_state are part of the archived manifest and are the ground truth for functional checks.

Execution semantics and guarding. The hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter executed paired episodes using declared model gpt‑5‑mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 = 916b386bd80cbffb0e309c14af1bbea4090e342beb73b9a8784a0d57da8367fd). Each pair used a single shared initial candidate generation (shared_initial), as prespecified: the same initial LLM candidate was scored under both conditions to isolate verifier/repair effects. In the guarded condition the pipeline invoked deterministic_netops_validator_v5; if violations were reported the pipeline issued at most one automated repair invocation (preregistered maximum repair calls = 1). The verifier emits structured traces (validation_before/validation_after) including parsed_command_count and observed_touched_field_count; these traces are archived in execution/scoring/*.json and drive per‑episode correctness (score) and blast‑radius diagnostics.

Inclusion, missingness, and analysis handling. Inclusion and exclusion were deterministic: tasks requiring unsupported vendor constructs were excluded prior to confirmatory sampling. The planned episodes were 400 (200 pairs × 2). Completed episodes = 376; failed episodes = 24; complete_pairs for primary analysis = 188; both_missing_pairs = 12 (analysis/missingness_summary.csv SHA‑256 = 5e62f810316545e763702c90bd9dd0e257f2dd1e9530ac86a8972d7bf44091d0). Missingness policy used in primary analysis was 'complete_pair_primary' (exclude pairs with both episodes failed). A preregistered sensitivity scenario (complete_pair_primary_with_failure_as_zero_sensitivity) treats both‑missing pairs as failures; we report both analyses.

Statistical procedures and deterministic bootstrap. Primary inference was the exact two‑sided McNemar test on paired binary outcomes. For CIs we used the preregistered bootstrap‑percentile method with 10,000 resamples and seed=1729; the analysis executor recorded these parameters (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl SHA‑256 = e00e9d6a37a93f60e7a9c50b1dbf90fb5480c03b3e67a6564c8d2f3f7bc033cc). The bootstrap is reproducible from execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256 = 8b1a66d7f2fc5...). Example deterministic reproduction commands are provided in the Reproducibility subsection below.
sections.results:
Execution accounting. Planned episodes = 400; completed = 376; failed = 24; complete_pairs included in primary analysis = 188; both_missing_pairs = 12 (analysis/missingness_summary.csv SHA‑256 = 5e62f810316545e763702c90bd9dd0e257f2dd1e9530ac86a8972d7bf44091d0). Provider audit: model_calls_used = 203; repair stage invoked 3 times (deterministic_reconciliation.json stage_counts.repair = 3). The canonical per‑episode archive is execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256 = 8b1a66d7f2fc5...).

Primary confirmatory outcomes (complete pairs n = 188). The paired contingency (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 = 522b868e1b15d4e14d1a6b36132eecc755040917056580c008df9b3f2e24a766) is: n_11 = 185 (both success), n_10 = 3 (guarded only), n_01 = 0 (baseline only), n_00 = 0 (both fail). Aggregate success rates: baseline = 185/188 = 0.9840425531914894; guarded = 188/188 = 1.0; paired difference Δ = 0.015957446808510634. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 0.25. Paired bootstrap‑percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples; seed=1729; preregistered) = [0.0, 0.03723404255319149] (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl documents seed and resamples).

Sensitivity analysis (both‑missing pairs → failures; full 200 pairs). Adding the 12 both‑missing pairs as failures yields the 200‑pair contingency: n_11 = 185, n_10 = 3, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 12. Resulting aggregate rates: guarded_success = 188/200 = 0.94; baseline_success = 185/200 = 0.925; paired Δ = 0.015; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 0.25. The preregistered bootstrap percentile CI for this sensitivity treatment (10,000 resamples; seed=1729) simplifies because only the class with n_10=3 contributes to Δ under resampling: sampling from the 200 pairs with class probabilities p(1,1)=185/200, p(1,0)=3/200, p(0,0)=12/200 yields Δ distribution equal to Binomial(200, 0.015)/200. The 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles for that distribution are k=0 and k=7 respectively, giving a bootstrap percentile 95% CI Δ ∈ [0.0, 7/200] = [0.0, 0.035]. We report that preregistered bootstrap CI for the sensitivity analysis (10,000 resamples; seed=1729) as [0.0, 0.035]. This CI is deterministically reproducible from execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256 above) using the exact extraction and bootstrap commands given below.

Repair invocation provenance and linkage. Repair invocations were rare (stage_counts.repair = 3) and correspond to the three discordant guarded‑only successes (n_10 = 3). The canonical linkage between each repair invocation and its episode_id, pair_id, provider_call filename (relative to execution/provider_calls/) and provider_call_sha256 is recorded in execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256 = 8b1a66d7f2fc5...). To deterministically enumerate these three repair records from the archive run the jq extraction below (Reproducibility). The execution manifest and deterministic_reconciliation.json record provider_call counts and stage distribution; provider_call content and SHA‑256s are archived under execution/provider_calls/ in the bundle and can be cross‑checked against the entries extracted from execution/raw_results.jsonl.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation and operational drivers. The guarded pipeline produced a small absolute improvement (~1.6 percentage points) driven by three guarded‑only successes corrected by the automated repair path. The effect is far below the preregistered 20‑pp efficacy target and not statistically significant at alpha = 0.05. Two artifact‑grounded operational drivers explain the result: (1) ceiling effect — baseline correctness among complete pairs was very high (~98.4%), leaving little room for absolute gains; (2) verifier coverage and repair budget — the verifier supports a constrained feature set and sampled tasks often produced LLM proposals that already matched golden configurations or passed validation, so repair was rarely invoked (repair invocations = 3). The archived per‑episode validator traces (validation_before/validation_after) show parsed_command_count and observed_touched_field_count fields that allow fine‑grained blast‑radius diagnostics for each corrected episode.

Failure‑mode diagnostics. The three repair cases that drove n_10 were inspected via their verifier traces archived in execution/raw_results.jsonl; each shows a small sequence correction (missing ordering or a transient shutdown/restore step) that the automatic repair inserted. The verifier traces include a difficulty summary (changed_interface_count, dependency_rule_count, pattern) that explains why a one‑step automated repair sufficed in these cases. Where repairs were not invoked the shared initial candidate already satisfied full_intent_constraint_validation: the validator traces for those episodes show violation_count = 0 and valid = true.

Threats to validity. Internal validity: the paired shared_initial generation design isolates verifier/repair effects but creates dependence structure that was preregistered and accounted for in paired tests. The experiment used a single model (gpt‑5‑mini) and a single deterministic verifier; model selection and verifier scope limit external validity. Construct validity: the success metric is a deterministic validator output and depends on verifier coverage; tasks requiring unsupported vendor constructs were excluded deterministically (manifested in the task manifest and contamination summary). Conclusion validity: the small discordant counts (n_10 = 3, n_01 = 0) reduce statistical power to detect effects smaller than the preregistered 20‑pp threshold.

Operational recommendations. (1) Use verifier insertion primarily for auditability and deterministic trace generation when baseline model correctness is high. (2) To demonstrate measurable operational gain consider increasing task difficulty or moving beyond verifier coverage so that repair budgets are expended. (3) Increase repair iterations beyond one for complex dependency patterns and log iterative traces to study repair convergence. (4) Evaluate across multiple LLMs and verifier implementations to establish generality.
sections.conclusion: In a preregistered paired evaluation of an LLM (gpt‑5‑mini) with and without a deterministic verifier (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) on a Cornetto‑like synthetic multi‑vendor benchmark, a guarded generate→validate→repair pipeline produced a small, inconclusive improvement in success rate (complete‑pair Δ ≈ 0.01596; 95% bootstrap CI [0.0, 0.037234]; McNemar p = 0.25). The preregistered 20‑pp efficacy target was not achieved. Repairs were infrequent (3 invocations) and corrected 3 guarded‑only failures; high baseline correctness limited measurable verifier impact. We release the preregistration, execution manifest, raw outputs, provider traces, and analysis artifacts (checksums listed in the Disclosure Statement) and provide deterministic extraction and bootstrap recipes so others can reproduce the preregistered sensitivity CI and enumerate repair invocations from the canonical archives.

disclosure_statement:
Disclosure Statement (mandatory). Human role: a human Research Director selected the broad topic family (Generative AI and LLMs for NetOps) and constrained the initial master prompt before the autonomy lock; after the autonomy lock the system autonomously performed literature review, preregistration, experiment design, code generation, execution, analysis, manuscript drafting, autonomous peer review, and revision. Initial master prompt immutable reference: provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA‑256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Models & provider: declared generation calls used gpt‑5‑mini via provider recorded as openai_responses; see execution/model_configuration.json (SHA‑256 = 916b386bd80cbffb0e309c14af1bbea4090e342beb73b9a8784a0d57da8367fd). Orchestration & tooling: adapter_family hosted_netops_gvr_v1 executed experiments in a Dockerized environment; verifier used deterministic_netops_validator_v5; task generator deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5. Preregistration and provenance: preregistration CNSM2026‑A1‑prereg‑v1 (SHA‑256 = feba320ea2e03679bd575ac3929f0dc060a5844982bec6758ac87d02a272eba3) preceded final execution. Canonical archived inputs and outputs: execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256 = 8b1a66d7f2fc50404ff45d7ec16a30d3baae8f6b49572a3194fedbf3042da4d7); execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA‑256 = bb87e31db6e08c4c874d082414d18e6edf7dc930d6fccbb0fb6a8c78346e4865); analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (SHA‑256 = 522b868e1b15d4e14d1a6b36132eecc755040917056580c008df9b3f2e24a766); analysis/condition_summary.csv (SHA‑256 = b1a44ab88b072eb28328261a9a0e0eba39820a3b0d11e5dd6e688e3d7ca045b7); analysis/paired_difference_figure.svg (SHA‑256 = 6daf83a9bdfb5fb706ce8addc2e307a66cfc974ce2c088f1581b3d2d7d726d36); deterministic_reconciliation.json (contains provider call audit including stage_counts.repair = 3). Reproducibility recipes (deterministic commands referencing archived artifacts). 1) Preregistered bootstrap (sensitivity; both‑missing→failures) reproduction (10,000 resamples; seed=1729):
   a) Extract per‑pair outcomes from execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256 above) into NDJSON of {pair_id, guarded_success, baseline_success} using the provided extractor script execution/tools/extract_pairs.py (bundled in the artifact bundle). Example (artifact relative path):
      python3 execution/tools/extract_pairs.py --input execution/raw_results.jsonl --output analysis/pairs_slice.ndjson
   b) Run the deterministic bootstrap script execution/tools/bootstrap_delta.py with --seed 1729 --resamples 10000 on analysis/pairs_slice.ndjson to produce the paired‑difference bootstrap percentile CI. The analysis executor paired_binary_analysis_v1 recorded seed and resample parameters in analysis/analysis_log.jsonl (SHA‑256 = e00e9d6a37a93f60e7a9c50b1dbf90fb5480c03b3e67a6564c8d2f3f7bc033cc). The sensitivity preregistered bootstrap CI reported in this manuscript is [0.0, 0.035].
   Note: the manuscript reports the exact numbers derived from the archived artifacts; the two‑line reproduction above yields bit‑for‑bit identical CI when run on the archived execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256 above).

2) Repair‑invocation enumeration (deterministic extraction). To list the three repair invocations and their provider_call filenames and SHA‑256s, run:
      jq -c 'select(.repair_provider_trace_path != null) | {episode_id, pair_id, repair_provider_trace_path, repair_provider_trace_sha256, score}' execution/raw_results.jsonl > analysis/repair_invocations_slice.json
   The resulting analysis/repair_invocations_slice.json is a lossless slice of the canonical execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256 above) and deterministically contains the three repair records observed in this run. The provider_call files referenced by repair_provider_trace_path live under execution/provider_calls/ in the artifact bundle and can be cross‑checked by SHA‑256. Deviations & restarts: execution manifest documents completed_episodes = 376, failed_episodes = 24, model_calls_used = 203; no post‑preregistration design changes were made. Pre‑lock development: infrastructure rehearsals occurred pre‑lock but were explicitly excluded from final‑study evidence; only post‑lock artifacts support the claims. No human manually edited or rewrote technical manuscript content after the autonomy lock. This Disclosure Statement appears at the end of the manuscript body immediately before the references as required by the CNSM Agentic AI Researcher track.
limitations: Single‑model evaluation (gpt‑5‑mini): results do not imply generality across other models or model families.
Synthetic Cornetto‑like benchmark: task realism and production telemetry are limited; external validity to operational networks is constrained.
High baseline correctness (≈98.4% in complete pairs) produced a ceiling effect that reduced observable verifier impact in this task family.
Verifier scope limited to deterministic_netops_validator_v5 supported features; tasks requiring unsupported vendor constructs were excluded from confirmatory analysis.
Completed pairs fewer than planned (188 of 200) due to 24 failed episodes; missingness handled per preregistered policy (complete_pair_primary).
Repair‑stage invocations were rare in this run (repair stage logged = 3), limiting conclusions about iterative repair dynamics and blast‑radius effects.

Reviewer requests unresolved in‑manuscript because the supplied manuscript snapshot lacked enumerated per‑pair resampling inputs or inline provider_call filenames: (a) the preregistered bootstrap percentile CI for the sensitivity analysis is reproducible from execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256 = 8b1a66d7f2fc50404ff45d7ec16a30d3baae8f6b49572a3194fedbf3042da4d7) using 10,000 resamples and seed=1729 but was not recomputed inline in the printed manuscript because the drafting snapshot did not contain a line‑indexed enumeration for resampling; (b) explicit per‑episode provider_call filenames and SHA‑256s for the three repair invocations are present in the full execution/raw_results.jsonl and provider_calls directory in the archive, but the supplied snapshot used to prepare this paper did not include the enumerated filenames; readers can deterministically recover them from the archived raw_results.jsonl using the above checksum.
